object.name: session_manager
object.description: Privileged interface for registering owned sessions. Only accessible to root clients.

c2s.name: create_session

description.summary: start registering a new session, returning an owning session object

c2s.description: Returns a session_management_session object bound to the calling connection. The client may stage optional fields before creating the session directly or through a delegated cgroup object.

object.name: session_management_session

description.summary: owning handle for a session created via create_session

object.description: Bound to the connection that created the session. Optional fields may be sent while the session is staged. Setting remote_host marks the session as remote. Once done has been sent, modifying staged fields or sending done again is a protocol error. Destroying this object tears down the session and its resources.

c2s.name: vt
c2s.description: Optional. Must be sent while staged. Defaults to 0 (not bound to a VT).

c2s.name: remote_host

description.summary: stage the remote host and mark the session as remote

c2s.description: Optional. Must be sent while staged.

c2s.name: class
c2s.description: Optional. Must be sent while staged. Defaults to user.

c2s.name: env
c2s.description: Optional. Must be sent while staged. May be sent multiple times.

c2s.name: done

description.summary: commit staged fields and create the session

c2s.description: Creates the session using uid and any staged vt/remote_host/env. The daemon responds with session_id, followed by done, or with error.

description.summary: session created, initial field dump complete
destroy this object and tear down the session

c2s.name: delegate_cgroup

description.summary: create a delegated cgroup for the session

c2s.description: Must be sent while staged. Creates the cgroup that will contain the session and returns an independent cgroup control object. The object exposes the path for a session supervisor such as dinit to pass to its --cgroup-path option and manage directly. The object owns the cgroup and its destruction destroys the cgroup.

object.name: session_management_cgroup
object.description: Control object for the cgroup created for a staged session. The object is usable independently by a session supervisor such as dinit, which can manage the cgroup using the delegated path. Destroying this object destroys the delegated cgroup.

s2c.name: path
s2c.description: Reports the exact path of the cgroup created for this object. The client may use this path to edit the cgroup directly.

c2s.name: controller
c2s.description: Must be sent before the session is committed. May be sent repeatedly. The requested controller name is made available to the delegated manager when supported by the kernel and permitted by daemon policy. The daemon does not enable the controller in the delegated cgroup; the delegated manager may enable it for its own child cgroups.

c2s.name: commit
c2s.description: Must be sent after all controller requests and before the owning session is committed. After this request, no further controller requests are allowed. The daemon creates and delegates the cgroup when the owning session is committed, then responds with path or error.

description.summary: destroy this object and its cgroup

value.name: user
value.summary: interactive login session owned by a user

value.name: greeter
value.summary: login prompt or display manager session

value.name: lock_screen
value.summary: screen locker session associated with an existing login

value.name: background
value.summary: non-interactive user session without an attached seat or VT

value.name: background_light
value.summary: lightweight background session excluded from idle shutdown accounting

value.name: manager_early
value.summary: early per-user service manager session created before a regular login
